content.text:
What changed and the responsibility split:

- **`Reporter.java`** — two-method interface: `reportSuccess(label, result)` and `reportError(label, errorMessage)`; both take plain strings so `Reporter` has no knowledge of arrays or exceptions — only presentation
- **`ConsoleReporter.java`** — the single `System.out.println` implementation; swapping to a file, JSON, or in-memory reporter for tests requires only a new class implementing this interface
- **`SortTestCase`** — retains `Arrays.toString` because converting an array to its string form is a data-formatting step that belongs with the caller, not the display layer; it now delegates both outcomes to the injected `Reporter` rather than printing directly
- **`Main`** — constructs one `ConsoleReporter` and shares it across all cases; the reporter is injected like the sorter, making it easy to swap presentation strategy globally from one place

- **`Reporter.java`** — two-method interface: `reportSuccess(label, result)` and `reportError(label, errorMessage)`; both take plain strings so `Reporter` has no knowledge of arrays or exceptions — only presentation
- **`ConsoleReporter.java`** — the single `System.out.println` implementation; swapping to a file, JSON, or in-memory reporter for tests requires only a new class implementing this interface
- **`SortTestCase`** — retains `Arrays.toString` because converting an array to its string form is a data-formatting step that belongs with the caller, not the display layer; it now delegates both outcomes to the injected `Reporter` rather than printing directly
- **`Main`** — constructs one `ConsoleReporter` and shares it across all cases; the reporter is injected like the sorter, making it easy to swap presentation strategy globally from one place
